title: The Sine, Cosine and Area Rules
seo_title: Grade 11 Sine, Cosine and Area Rules Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Prove and apply the sine, cosine and area rules; solve problems in two dimensions using the sine, cosine and area rules.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 11 worksheets: the area rule, the sine rule, the cosine rule and problems in two dimensions. 100 questions with memos.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Area rule: Area = ½ab sin C (two sides and the angle between them).
  • Sine rule: asin A = bsin B = csin C.
  • Cosine rule: a² = b² + c² − 2bc cos A (two sides and the angle between them, or three sides).
  • Draw the triangle and label the side opposite each angle with the same letter.

Examples

Example

b = 7, c = 9, A = 40°

a² = 49 + 81 − 126 cos 40°

Answer: a = 5,8

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
The wrong paira goes with A, the angle opposite it.
No square rootThe cosine rule gives a².
Forgetting ½Area = ½ab sin C.

faq.q: When do I use the cosine rule?
faq.a: With two sides and the included angle, or three sides.

faq.q: When do I use the sine rule?
faq.a: With a side and its opposite angle.

items.q: Find the two angles between 0° and 180° for which sin θ = 0,4067. Give your answers correct to 1 decimal place.
items.e: sin−1 0,4067 = 24,0°. Sine is also positive in the second quadrant: 180° − 24,0° = 156,0°. θ = 24,0° or θ = 156,0°.

Two lookout towers are 180 m apart. A fire is seen at angles of 39° and 68° from the line joining the towers. How far is the fire from the first tower (the one with the 39° angle), to the nearest metre?
items.e: The third angle is 73°. The side from the first tower to the fire is opposite the 68° angle: d = 180 × sin 68° ÷ sin 73° = 175 m.

items.q: You know two sides and the angle between them. Which law finds the third side?
items.e: SAS gives no matching side-angle pair, so use the Cosine rule. Cosine rule.

items.q: A triangle has sides a = 10, b = 17 and c = 19. Find the largest angle, ∠C, to the nearest tenth of a degree.
What does the Cosine rule become when ∠C = 90°?
items.e: cos 90° = 0, so c² = a² + b². The Pythagorean theorem.

items.q: A triangle has sides a = 13, b = 14 and c = 19. Find the largest angle, ∠C, to the nearest tenth of a degree.
You know all three sides of a triangle. Which law finds an angle?
items.e: SSS: rearrange the Cosine rule to find the cosine of an angle. Cosine rule.

items.q: A triangle has sides 8 cm, 9 cm and 12 cm. Find the largest angle, correct to 1 decimal place.
items.e: The largest angle is opposite the longest side, 12 cm. cos C = (8² + 9² − 12²) ÷ (2 × 8 × 9) = 0,0069, so C = 89,6°.

items.q: In a park, paths form a triangle PQR. ∠P = 39°, ∠Q = 47° and QR = 38 m. Find PR, correct to 1 decimal place.
items.e: QR is opposite ∠P and PR is opposite ∠Q. Sine rule: PR ÷ sin 47° = 38 ÷ sin 39°, so PR = 44,2 m.
